verdict.call: Hold existing -- no fresh capital at spot, wait for the July 30 print
verdict.note: Internal weighted estimate is 5.7% above consensus but 0.9% below spot. This is the inverted case: the sell-side average target sits 6.25% BELOW the market price, so there is no valuation gap to harvest -- the gap is between price and every anchor.

key_finding.summary: Apple is repurchasing stock at the highest multiple in the history of its buyback program, and the program's efficiency has quietly halved. Buyback yield is 2.39%, a 5-year low, versus 4.3% in FY2022; the record $100B authorization now retires only ~2.0% of a $4.99T market cap. Cook has overseen ~$853B of repurchases retiring 44% of shares, but that average was struck far below 41x earnings. Alongside it: insider ownership is 0.06%, there have been zero open-market purchases by any named officer at any price, and Cook's only 2026 transaction was a 10b5-1 sale of 64,949 shares at $250.73-$256.10 on April 2 -- roughly 33% below spot -- five months before handing the CEO role to John Ternus.
key_finding.caveat: The yield compression is arithmetic, not a policy retreat: the stock is up 59% in 52 weeks while the board raised the authorization to $100B, and TTM FCF of $129.17B funds it comfortably on $61.88B net cash. Cook's sale was mechanical under a plan adopted May 24, 2024; he retains 3,280,418 shares (~$1.1B) and stays on as executive chairman. And the buyback is not the earnings engine -- Q2 FY26 EPS grew 22% on 17% revenue with share count down only 2.4%, so operating leverage did the work.

sector_context.name: Consumer hardware / megacap technology
sector_context.narrative: The anti-AI-capex trade. The 2026 Magnificent Seven have been punished for spending -- the cohort is committing as much as $725B to AI capex this year, with Alphabet alone guiding to $205B -- while Apple sat the race out and rented Gemini from Google for roughly $1B a year. Apple is up ~24% YTD and ~59% over 52 weeks, overtook Nvidia as the world's most valuable company on July 18, and briefly touched $5T intraday on July 28. Over the same trailing year Microsoft is down ~23% and the semiconductor index has fallen into a bear market. Capital discipline is what is being re-rated, not growth.
sector_context.relative_positioning: Apple is ~13% of XLK and its second-largest holding behind Nvidia, so the sector proxy is a levered version of the same bet, not a hedge. The intra-cohort positioning has fully inverted: Apple was megacap's cheap ex-growth name a year ago and is now the most expensive on nearly every anchor (41.23x trailing P/E, 30.84x EV/EBITDA, 38.67x P/FCF) while carrying the slowest 3Y consensus EPS growth in the group at 13.37%. The names still trading at a discount are the heavy AI spenders -- discounted for precisely the reason Apple is not.

elevator_pitch: Apple has been re-rated for what it did NOT do: it skipped the AI capex race, rented Gemini for ~$1B a year, and is up 59% over 52 weeks while the spenders were punished -- overtaking Nvidia and briefly touching $5T on July 28.

But roughly 60% of that return is multiple expansion, not earnings: trailing P/E moved from ~31x to 41.23x while TTM EPS grew ~20%. The 47-analyst consensus target of $318.81 now sits 6.25% BELOW spot.

The business is genuinely accelerating -- Q2 FY26 revenue +17%, record $30.98B Services, 49.3% gross margin, Greater China +28% -- but the July 30 print is Cook's last, carries the first read on the memory-cost squeeze, and the stock is at an all-time high with RSI 68.9.
bull_case: Capital discipline is now a re-rating asset: the megacap cohort is committing up to $725B to AI capex in 2026 while Apple's TTM capex is $11.05B (~2.4% of revenue), converting 28.6% of revenue straight into free cash flow.
The business accelerated into the re-rating -- Q2 FY26 revenue +17% (from +16% in Q1), EPS +22%, gross margin a multi-year-high 49.3%, and Q3 guidance of 14-17% against a 9.5% analyst forecast.
Services is the margin engine: a record $30.98B, +16.3% YoY, and the primary driver of sequential gross-margin expansion per CFO Parekh.
Greater China flipped from the chronic bear point to a tailwind -- +28% in Q2 and +33% for the first half of FY2026, both March-quarter records, against a China smartphone market down 4.3%.
The Gemini deal converts Apple's most-cited weakness into a ~$1B annual operating expense instead of a $100B+ capex program: frontier AI distribution without owning the depreciation.

Returns on capital are structurally unmatched -- ROIC 104.33%, ROE 141.47%, net cash $61.88B, Altman Z-Score 10.64, and $129.17B TTM FCF funding a $100B authorization plus 14 straight years of dividend growth.
bear_case: The 47-analyst consensus target of $318.81 sits 6.25% below spot -- the street already thinks the stock has overshot, and Citi's $365 is an outlier, not the median.
Roughly 60% of the 59% 52-week return is multiple expansion, not earnings: trailing P/E moved from ~31x to 41.23x on ~20% TTM EPS growth. PEG is 3.24 against 3Y consensus EPS growth of just 13.37%.
EV/EBITDA is 30.84x versus 25.77x on May 1, 2026 -- roughly 20% of multiple expansion in under three months with no change in the underlying earnings trajectory.

The July 30 print delivers the first financial read on the AI-driven memory shortage. Apple already raised Mac and iPad prices in June while holding iPhone pricing, which means the cost lands in gross margin rather than revenue.

The ~$20B annual Google default payment -- estimated at 4-6% of Apple profit at near-100% margin -- runs only until at least September 2026, and the Mehta remedy caps defaults at 12 months with no exclusivity, forcing an annual re-auction. The DOJ appeal is live at the D.C. Circuit.
That same remedy language explicitly covers Gemini distribution, so the AI partnership that fixed the Siri problem sits inside the antitrust perimeter rather than outside it.

This is a CEO handover into a record multiple: Cook's July 30 call is his last, Ternus takes over September 1 and has never run a print, and insider ownership is 0.06% with zero open-market officer purchases at any price.
The technical setup is stretched -- price at an all-time high, RSI 68.9, and 22.9% above the 200-day MA at $276.79 -- into a Fed decision and an earnings print inside the same 48 hours.
thesis_summary.decision_question: Is 'capital discipline' a durable re-rating or a rotation that reverses the moment AI capex starts showing returns? Open question: does the July 30 print -- Cook's last, and the first quantification of the memory-cost squeeze -- justify 41x, or is the market paying a record price for the one megacap that explicitly is not building the thing it is paying up for?

valuation.reverse_dcf_note: Regular DCF was abandoned on the same two rules that killed it for NOW: terminal value is 78% of enterprise value, and a +/-5pp WACC move swings fair value by well over 50%. Reverse DCF at a 10.11% WACC and 2.5% terminal growth: the current $4.93T enterprise value implies a ~29% 5-year FCF CAGR off a $129.17B base -- against 3Y consensus forecasts of 10.70% revenue growth and 13.37% EPS growth. This is the exact inverse of NOW: where NOW's price embedded a fear discount below consensus, Apple's price embeds a growth rate the sell side does not forecast. Scenario multiples are therefore the primary layer, applied to ~$500B NTM revenue implied by the 9.97x forward P/S.

positive: July 30 Q3 FY26 print: Services holding above 15% and gross margin above 48% despite memory costs
iPhone 17 renewal cycle extending, plus the Klarna device-leasing program launched July 28 converting sticker price into a monthly payment
Greater China sustaining positive growth against a smartphone market down 4.3%
A rebuilt, Gemini-powered Siri actually shipping and proving competitive -- the largest outstanding execution item
Continued rotation out of AI-capex names into capital-discipline names, with the semis index already in a bear market
Ternus transition landing cleanly on September 1, plus a first capital-return update under the new CEO
negative: Memory-chip cost inflation compressing product gross margin below 47% on the July 30 guide
Loss or repricing of the ~$20B Google default payment as the D.C. Circuit appeal proceeds and the September 2026 term approaches
10Y at 4.62-4.64% into a July 29 FOMC decision where market pricing is unusually split -- a hawkish outcome compresses a 41x multiple first
Any Siri / Apple Intelligence slip that turns 'capital discipline' back into 'AI laggard'
Softening smartphone and PC end markets, plus the OpenAI trade-secret litigation Apple filed
Multiple mean reversion alone: EV/EBITDA reverting from 30.84x to the 25.77x of May 1 is a ~16% price move with no fundamental change

risk_management.thesis_changing_risk: Two consecutive quarters of consolidated gross margin below 47% would confirm the memory-cost squeeze is structural rather than transitory, and would remove the earnings-quality justification for a 41x multiple. The faster version is the Google default payment: a court-forced repricing removes roughly 4-6% of profit at near-100% margin, landing entirely on the Services multiple the whole re-rating rests on.

checklist: Gross margin: confirm >= 48% holding through the memory-cost cycle, or break if < 47% for a second quarter
Services growth: confirm >= 15%, or break if < 12%
Google default payment: confirm the arrangement survives the September 2026 term and the D.C. Circuit appeal intact, or break on any repricing
Siri / Apple Intelligence: confirm a shipped, competitive Gemini-powered assistant, or the 'discipline' framing reverts to 'AI laggard'
Ternus transition: first full quarter under the new CEO -- watch for any change in capital-return cadence or guidance style
Multiple: confirm EPS revisions are catching up to 41x, or treat further expansion without revisions as distribution
